title: Policy orchestration and plan validators for Private/VPC Terraform pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a policy-orchestration layer and immutable plan validators in the Terraform CI/CD pipelines for Private/VPC deployments. This ticket covers pre-apply linting, plan-time validation using OPA/Conftest, storage and signing of plan artifacts, and a small on-apply health-check harness for post-deploy verification.

Motivation: We've had multiple near-misses on VPC upgrades where CIDR changes or inadvertent public ingress were introduced via quick patch PRs. For Private deployments we must make upgrades safer by catching risky changes at plan time and providing automatic, auditable gates before apply.

Scope:
- Add a pipeline step that produces a machine-readable Terraform plan (TF JSON) for every PR and push to main.
- Run Conftest (rego) + OPA policies against plan JSON to flag changes to: subnets, route tables, security group ingress/egress, KMS key policies, IAM role inline policies, and S3/bucket ACLs.
- Build an "immutable-plan validator" that enforces allowed-change whitelists per module. If a PR's plan modifies pinned module versions, the validator fails.
- Store signed plan artifacts in the artifact store (GCS) with a checksum and link in the pipeline log.
- Provide a plan-diff summarizer comment on the PR with the list of resources added/changed/deleted and policy violations.
- Introduce a policy orchestration config (YAML) in infra/ci that maps policies to pipeline environments (e.g., dev, staging, prod).
- Require manual approval for plans that are labelled high-risk by policy score or that touch protected modules.
- On successful apply to staging/dedicated test VPC, execute a lightweight health-check job (Bash/Python) that validates basic connectivity: control plane -> worker nodes, sample egress to internal services, and KMS encryption end-to-end for a test object.
- Schedule a drift detection job (weekly) for private VPCs and surface results in Console-Observability dashboards (link to next ticket).

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We'll use Conftest for fast feedback in PRs; OPA rego policies will be the canonical source in infra/opa/policies. Conftest provides easy local testing.
- To avoid long-running PR checks, the plan validator runs a lightweight subset of rules (fast-fail). Full policy evaluation will run in the gating job post-plan and before apply.
- Storing signed plan artifacts increases cost and storage footprint but provides an auditable upgrade trail for compliance. We will TTL artifacts after 180 days.
- Manual approvals add overhead; therefore we will tune risk thresholds so only genuinely risky changes require human intervention.

Notes on implementation:
- Pipeline changes will live in .github/workflows/terraform-ci.yaml and in Jenkins shared libs for on-prem runners.
- Rego location: infra/opa/policies/vpc/* (examples: vpc_changes.rego, sg_ingress.rego, kms_policies.rego).
- Sample PR with prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4897 (contains conftest rules and plan summarizer scripts).
- Design doc: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4-redwood-iac-policy-orchestration (internal).
- Console ticket to surface policy scores: PM-1182 (follow-up).

Acceptance criteria (see separate field for machine-readable list):
- Every terraform PR produces a plan JSON and a Conftest result in the PR checks.
- Violations block the apply and provide actionable messages in the PR.
- Plans are uploaded and signed to GCS with a checksum and ttl metadata.
- Manual approval workflow exists for high-risk plans and is enforced in the pipeline.
- Post-apply health-check job runs and reports success/failure in the pipeline logs.

Retention and observability:
- Policy evaluation metrics (violations per rule, per repo, per author) are emitted to prometheus and a dashboard is provisioned by SRE (separate ticket).

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag the lightweight plan validator on infra repos (2 weeks).
2) Iterate rego rules with Security and SRE; reduce false positives (1 week).
3) Enforce in staging and require manual approval for prod-only changes (2 weeks).
4) Extend to dedicated customer workspaces and add TTL/archival (1 week).
